text: Usman Tariq, a Karachi grocery wholesaler, deposited a total of PKR 28,890,000 in cash between 4 March and 29 March 2026, with 23 separate cash‑deposit transactions exceeding PKR 2,000,000 each. The deposits were made at the Hyderabad Main Branch, all recorded as "Cash (over the counter)" and show no corresponding invoices or business justification. In parallel, the account made three identical out‑flows of PKR 7,959,000 to Metro FMCG Distributors (Synthetic Bank C) on 7, 14, 21, and 28 March, each labelled "STOCK INVOICE" but with no supporting documentation. The pattern of large, frequent cash deposits followed by large out‑flows to the same counterparty suggests possible structuring to avoid reporting thresholds and potential money‑laundering. The customer’s declared monthly turnover (PKR 84,000,000) and income (PKR 1,400,000) do not align with the volume of cash activity. The synthetic nature of the case and the absence of any legitimate business explanation warrant filing a Suspicious Transaction Report.
